title: Building Lucky Flock with Claude, Codex and PixelLab: my wins, my misses, and a demo you can play in your browser
author: Toamig
selftext:
Hi all, I'm a solo developer making a cozy pizel-art roguelite game about counting sheep to put nightmares to sleep. The idea started with a desire to create a game where I could explore math as the core mechanic, so in this game you line your sheep on a fence with tools that change the count, and you send the line towards a nightmare. Landing a number exactly gives a small bonus, but you do not have to.   
The video is real footage of the game.

Since this sub is about how we use AI, here is the honest split. The pixel art was generated with AI tools (PixelLab and ChatGPT) and then selected and edited by me, and the code was written with AI assistance (Claude Code and Codex). The design, the rules and the balance are mine, and nothing is generated while you play.

**What has worked:**

* **Code, fast:** Claude Code and Codex write code quickly, and git worktrees and branches let me run experiments side by side and throw away what doesn't work.
* **Art:** PixelLab and ChatGPT got me decent pixel art, with a few extra generations, sharper prompts or a few pixels fixed by hand.
* **Juice:** I named games with a similar feel to what I wanted, and Opus or Fable used them as reference for springs, squash and big moments.
* **Design reviews:** it checks my design against known frameworks and gathers what players complain about in Steam reviews of similar games.
* **Video and marketing:** reach is still small, but the clips keep improving. I get clips filmed by scripts driving the real game, edited with ffmpeg and Remotion, with ElevenLabs voiceovers.

**Where the AI was weaker:**

* **UI:** clipped text and squeezed panels, and the game gets very wordy and confusing without constant correction and human iteration.
* **Tone:** clever nerdy jokes to explain the rules that I personally dislike.
* **Audio:** I haven't tried a dedicated AI audio tool tried yet. Claude and Codex make mechanical or synth-like sound that doesn't fit this game, often place or pick sound effects wrong or out of sync, and are shallow at audio editing and polish.
* **Balancing:** there are a lot of variables and factors, and it doesn't really get how to simulate the players and playstyles this game brings out. Its simulated players can tell me a lot, but they don't play like people do, so balance still comes down to real play and my own judgement.

The demo plays in your browser on itch.io, no download needed: https://toamig.itch.io/lucky-flock

I would love feedback on the game and on how I describe the AI side. Does this split read as honest to you? Thanks for reading 🐏🎲

comments.author: ArtificialBeingsInc
comments.body:
I tried the first night of the older itch build: sending sheep 3 + 4 at the 7 nightmare gave me an EXACT, which made the goal click. I initially pressed the prominent Send button before realizing I needed to tap the nightmare to aim first; the hint appeared at the bottom. If the current build works the same way, a “choose a nightmare” cue beside Send could make that step clearer.



The itch page says this playable build is older than the screenshots, so I’d mention that next to the demo link here too. I haven’t played the newer build. Your AI breakdown reads clearly to me about what the tools made and where your own design and editing came in.

replies.author: Toamig
replies.body:
Thank you so much for the feedback and even more for trying the game! 🙏  
I'll make an edit to the post mentioning that.   
  
What did you think about the core loop? Did you feel like continuing to play?

replies.author: ArtificialBeingsInc
replies.body: The 3 + 4 match gave me a clear little puzzle, and I was curious to see what happens when the total goes over and how multiplication changes the choice. I stopped after that first tutorial match, though, so I can’t honestly judge whether the wider loop stays engaging yet.

comments.author: stolenyourgf
comments.body: fwiw the thing that bit me with pixellab stuff was the pixel size drifting a bit between generations, so i drop everything on one grid at 1x and look at it side by side before importing. did you end up fixing much of that by hand?

replies.author: Toamig
replies.body: I didn't have that problem with pixellab but it does happen when I'm using other AIs with image generation capabilities. The good thing about pixel lab with that you can chose the resolution of your output: e.g. 16x16 px; 32x32px; 128x128ox etc so it gives me what I want exactly. I feel like pixel lab is very accurate for pixel art generation, definitely worth the price
